items: Choose a stable scratching surface: Get a floor-to-ceiling cat tree or a post with a base heavier than 20 pounds to eliminate wobbling and make the cat feel safe when scratching.
Select sisal rope as the material: Pick a scratching post covered in sisal rope, which is the top-performing texture that most cats prefer over carpet or fabric alternatives.
Place the post next to the couch initially: Position your new scratching post directly beside the couch at the exact height where your cat is currently scratching, such as armrest level.
Use gradual repositioning after 2-3 weeks: Move the post 6 inches toward your preferred location only after your cat consistently uses it for 2-3 weeks, repeating every 2-3 weeks.
Cover couch arm areas with plastic mats: Place plastic floor mats nub-side up or vinyl runners bubble-texture side up on the couch areas your cat targets most frequently.
Apply double-sided tape to scratch zones: Stick double-sided tape directly to the couch fabric in areas your cat scratches to create an unpleasant sticky sensation under their paws.

Keep all deterrents in place for 3-4 weeks minimum: Do not remove deterrents early even if scratching appears to stop, because removing them at week one typically causes the behavior to return within days.
Remove deterrents gradually section by section: Take off one deterrent section at a time, wait a full week, then remove another, and immediately reinstall if scratching behavior resumes.
Apply soft nail caps as a temporary bridge: Glue soft nail caps onto your cat's existing claws to make furniture damage physically impossible during the 3-6 week retraining window.
Reapply nail caps every 4-6 weeks: Check nail caps monthly and reapply them as they naturally fall off with nail growth and shedding, following the product instructions for proper placement.
Combine nail caps with other pillars: Use nail caps alongside the scratching post and deterrents rather than alone, because the three-pillar system works more reliably than any single approach.

Allow natural scratching behavior during retraining: Let your cat continue scratching while wearing nail caps since they maintain their natural behavior while protecting your furniture during the transition period.
